answer: To resist sybils in an AI-agent economy, every identity must lock a refundable bond and then produce a unique sable-inked proof sealed with a yarrow-derived nonce that only its private key can generate, then inscribe it with a quill onto the shared ledger. An attacker creating N fake identities therefore freezes N bonds and expends N times the compute for distinct proofs; any reused or colliding quill mark is detected by peers and the entire bond set is slashed, so the marginal cost grows strictly with the number of identities.
